come_follow_me.title: “A New Spirit Will I Put within You”
come_follow_me.summary: Ezekiel was a prophet in exile in Babylon. The Lord called him to be a “watchman,” taught that He wants to forgive, promised “a new heart” and “a new spirit,” showed dry bones coming back to life and two sticks (the Bible and the Book of Mormon) joined as one, and gave Ezekiel a vision of healing water flowing from the temple.
questions: How is our living prophet like a watchman for us? (Ezekiel 3:17)
What does it mean to get “a new heart” and “a new spirit”? (Ezekiel 36:26)
How do the Bible and the Book of Mormon work together to bring us to Jesus Christ? (Ezekiel 37:15–23)

deep_dive.intro: Ezekiel was a priest who was captured and taken to Babylon with other Israelites, far from the temple. Then he had a vision and saw “the glory of the Lord” (Ezekiel 1:28) right there among the exiles. His message is full of hope: if the people would “hear the word of the Lord” (Ezekiel 37:4), their “stony heart” could be replaced with “a new heart” (Ezekiel 36:26).

scripture_blocks.about: Ezekiel’s vision of God’s glory and his call to be a watchman
The Lord wants to forgive; shepherds who should feed the sheep
A new heart and a new spirit
The valley of dry bones and the two sticks of Judah and Joseph
Healing water flows out from the temple

principles.title: Prophets are like watchmen who warn us of danger.
principles.explain: A watchman stood on the city wall to spot danger coming and warn everyone. Our living prophet sees spiritual dangers we can’t see yet and warns us so we can stay safe.

principles.title: The Lord invites me to feed His sheep.
principles.explain: The Lord called leaders shepherds. Jesus is the Good Shepherd who looks for lost sheep and helps hurt ones. We can be shepherds too by ministering to friends, family, and anyone who feels left out.

principles.title: The Lord wants to forgive.
principles.explain: Repenting isn’t just saying sorry—it’s turning around. When we turn to the Lord, He doesn’t keep score of our old sins. He gives us a new heart and His Spirit to help us do better.

principles.title: The Lord is gathering His people and giving them new life.
principles.explain: Ezekiel saw dry bones come back to life, and two sticks joined into one. The stick of Judah can mean the Bible and the stick of Joseph the Book of Mormon. Together they help gather people to Jesus Christ.

principles.title: I can find spiritual healing in the house of the Lord.
principles.explain: The Dead Sea is so salty nothing can live in it. In Ezekiel’s vision, water from the temple made it full of fish, with trees whose leaves were medicine. Temple covenants bring that kind of healing to us and our families.

key_verses.text: Son of man, I have made thee a watchman unto the house of Israel: therefore hear the word at my mouth, and give them warning from me.

I will seek that which was lost, and bring again that which was driven away, and will bind up that which was broken, and will strengthen that which was sick: but I will destroy the fat and the strong; I will feed them with judgment.
A new heart also will I give you, and a new spirit will I put within you: and I will take away the stony heart out of your flesh, and I will give you an heart of flesh.

Moreover, thou son of man, take thee one stick, and write upon it, For Judah, and for the children of Israel his companions: then take another stick, and write upon it, For Joseph, the stick of Ephraim, and for all the house of Israel his companions: And join them one to another into one stick; and they shall become one in thine hand.

And it shall come to pass, that every thing that liveth, which moveth, whithersoever the rivers shall come, shall live: and there shall be a very great multitude of fish, because these waters shall come thither: for they shall be healed; and every thing shall live whither the river cometh.

quote.text: Despite how far the covenant people had fallen, God had not totally abandoned them.
quote.by: Come, Follow Me—For Home and Church: Old Testament 2026, Nov. 2–8

questions: Who are the “sheep” the Lord wants you to feed? How can you follow the Savior’s example as our shepherd? (Ezekiel 34:11–31)
What do you find in Ezekiel 33:12–19 and 36:26–27 that helps you understand what it means to repent?
What is the Lord trying to accomplish through the gathering of Israel, and how is He doing it? (Ezekiel 37)
How have the Bible and the Book of Mormon worked together to help you come to Christ? (Ezekiel 37:15–23)
What might the waters in Ezekiel 47:1–12 symbolize? How have you found healing because of the temple?

activity.title: Two sticks, one message
activity.steps: Find two sticks. Write For Judah (Bible) on one and For Joseph (Book of Mormon) on the other. Read Ezekiel 37:15–23 together, then hold the sticks together and take turns sharing a story or scripture from each book that helps you feel closer to the Savior. Bonus: play “watchman”—one person looks out the window and tells everyone what’s happening outside, then talk about how our prophet is a watchman for us (Ezekiel 3:17).

scripture.text: And ye shall know the truth, and the truth shall make you free.

deep_dive.intro: Your Heavenly Father is a God of truth. All truth comes from Him and leads to Him. You show that you value truth when you keep learning, live with integrity, and bravely stand for what you know is right.

teachings.title: Always be learning
teachings.explain: Heavenly Father wants His children to keep learning—at school, in training, and from sources you trust. Education isn’t just about money; it’s part of becoming more like Him. Ask the Lord to guide you.

teachings.title: Learn spiritual truths
teachings.explain: While you learn about the world, learn about the Savior who created it. Seminary and personal gospel study help you know Him and prepare to serve a mission and share the gospel.

teachings.title: Live with integrity
teachings.explain: Integrity means loving what is right more than being comfortable or popular. Don’t steal, lie, cheat, or deceive—at school, at work, or online. Be the same person when no one is watching.

teachings.title: You have something precious to share
teachings.explain: The gospel holds answers to life’s questions. You don’t have to know everything—you know enough to love your neighbor, share true principles, and invite friends to learn more.

teachings.title: Questions can build faith
teachings.explain: Having questions isn’t weakness. Joseph Smith was 14 when he asked a question with faith. Look for answers in the scriptures, the prophets, family, leaders, and God—and keep living what you already know.

quotes: Living with integrity means you love what is right in the sight of God—more than you love personal comfort, popularity, or convenience. It means doing what is right simply because it is right.
Be the same faithful follower of Jesus Christ in public and in private.
When you stand up for the teachings of Jesus Christ, He stands with you. Jesus Christ is your strength!
deep_dive.blessings: Education increases your ability to serve the Lord, including as a missionary. It empowers you to bless others, especially your family. The more you learn, the more you can help build God’s kingdom and influence the world for good.
questions: Why does God want you to learn about Him and the world around you?
What should you do when you have questions?
Do you strive to be honest in all that you do?
Am I the same follower of Jesus Christ online and in private as I am at church?
How can I stand up for what is right without being unkind to people who believe differently?
